notes: בְּיָדֶךָ is the predicate of a verbless clause, so the supplied *is* joins the preposition heading it (rule 49).
מֵעִם → *from* fuses under rule 30's one-English-word condition, headed on מִן, whose sense the word carries.
אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ again puts the *hath* on the verbless clause's possessive לְ and the subject pronoun on its suffix (rule 43).
